messages:
maria: Heads up — planning to roll out the routing policy change for v2 models in the 14:00-15:00 UTC change window. Need final thumbs and async approvals.

deploy-bot: @maria noted change window 2026-03-19 14:00-15:00 UTC. Canaries: 2% -> 10% over 30m, guard: latency-error spike thresholds set. Run `jobs/rollout/v2-routing` to start.

aj: I reviewed the canary config. Two questions: 1) can we have a manual pause at 5%? 2) Does the rollout respect quota caps for free-tier customers?

maria: yes to manual pause — adding a step. Quotas: config routes to fallback model if quota exhausted, but need to confirm cost-accounting tag in the telemetry. @nate can you confirm?

nate: Confirmed — telemetry will include cost_account and route_id. We need to enable the per-route quota guard though, otherwise traffic could exceed reserved capacity during burst. I'll flip the guard on before rollout.

kelly: FYI, console UX for the rollout page will show a live traffic split chart and the canary guard state. I pushed a tiny UI patch that surfaces the manual pause button and the kill-switch. No prod deploy yet.

maria: Great. One more ops ask: the deploy-bot should require two approvals for this change (platform + infra) because it touches routing and infra autoscale. Can we enforce that?

deploy-bot: Approval check: 1 required (owner), 2 recommended. To override, use `/deploy approve --override` and include justification. Audit event will be recorded.

aj: hmm can we change the bot to enforce 2 approvals for rollouts tagged `infra-impact`? That's our previous policy for canary-sensitive changes.

nate: I can update the approval policy in the workflow. Quick diff: `rollout_policy.yaml` add `required_approvals: 2` when `infra-impact: true`. Should be safe; will run tests.

kelly: Also adding a small acceptance test that checks the console shows the approval count and blocks the primary 'start' button until approvals >= required.

maria: Sounds good. Timeline: nate flips quota guard and approval policy at 13:30 UTC, kelly deploys the UI at 13:40 (can be hotfix), then we start rollout at 14:00.

sre-oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall rotation — @nate oncall at 13:00-21:00 UTC. Incident channels prepped, alert thresholds copied to #incidents.

aj: I'll be monitoring traces/dashboards for 30m post 10% step. Which dashboards should we watch?

nate: Watch `routes.latency.p95`, `model.errors.rate`, `inference.kvcache.hitrate` and the new `cost.per_token.estimated`. I'll pin links in the thread.

maria: If anyone sees >2x p95 or errors >0.5% absolute increase, hit pause and call it. Also manual rollback plan: `/deploy rollback jobs/rollout/v2-routing --to=stable-2026-03-17` — tested in staging.

deploy-bot: To start the rollout once approvals are met, run:```/deploy start jobs/rollout/v2-routing --change-window=2026-03-19T14:00Z```

maria: Thanks. Final ask: aj please add a small canary eval set to the monitoring job — a few prompts that are sensitive to hallucination so we catch quality regressions early.

aj: On it. I'll push evals by EOD and tag the rollout with `quality-checks:true`.

maria: Perfect. If no objections by 13:20 UTC we proceed with the plan. :thumbsup:

kelly: LGTM from UX side.

nate: LGTM infra, I'll flip the guards and approval policy at 13:30.

maria: thanks team — will update this thread when the first approval lands.
